test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 10 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: There are three cups of mixture of milk and water in ratio 4 ∶ 5, 5 ∶ 6, 9 ∶ 7. 36 liters of first and 44 liters of second cup are taken. How much quantity from third cup is to be taken so that final mixture from the three cups will have milk and water in ratio 1 ∶ 1?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Milk in **Cup 1** = 36 × (4/9) = 16 L | Water = 36 − 16 = 20 L

Milk in **Cup 2** = 44 × (5/11) = 20 L | Water = 44 − 20 = 24 L

Let x be quantity from **Cup 3**: Milk = (9/16)x, Water = (7/16)x

For 1 : 1 ratio: Total Milk = Total Water ⇒ 16 + 20 + (9/16)x = 20 + 24 + (7/16)x

36 + (9/16)x = 44 + (7/16)x ⇒ (2/16)x = 8 ⇒ x = 64 L

**∴ The correct answer is 64 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio 1 = 4 : 5, Ratio 2 = 5 : 6, Ratio 3 = 9 : 7. Quantities taken = 36 L, 44 L, and x L. Final Ratio = 1 : 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/813ac7f5e8a122435a35bc646c0875ff55de0ab9170c71f3467b390a33c42a9a.png] 

⇒ **Milk from Cup 1** = 36 × (4 / (4+5)) = 36 × (4/9) = 16 L

⇒ **Water from Cup 1** = 36 − 16 = 20 L

⇒ **Milk from Cup 2** = 44 × (5 / (5+6)) = 44 × (5/11) = 20 L

⇒ **Water from Cup 2** = 44 − 20 = 24 L

⇒ Let quantity from **Cup 3** be x litres. Milk = 9x/16, Water = 7x/16

⇒ **Total Milk** = 16 + 20 + 9x/16 = 36 + 9x/16

⇒ **Total Water** = 20 + 24 + 7x/16 = 44 + 7x/16

⇒ Since final ratio is 1 : 1, Total Milk = Total Water

⇒ 36 + 9x/16 = 44 + 7x/16

⇒ 9x/16 − 7x/16 = 44 − 36

⇒ 2x/16 = 8 ⇒ x/8 = 8 ⇒ x = 64 L

**∴ The correct answer is 64 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Mixture Components

If a mixture has components A and B in ratio m : n, then the quantity of A in Q volume is Q × m/(m+n).

Alligation Method

Used for mixing two items. For three items, calculate the weighted average of the first two and then alligate with the third.

1 : 1 Ratio Property

A final ratio of 1 : 1 implies that the total absolute quantities of the two components must be equal.</p
